title: MemoryMesh
subtitle: Conflict-aware AI memory engine
summary: A persistent memory system that turns natural-language statements into structured facts, retrieves semantically related memories, and reasons about how new information relates to what is already known.
bullets: Built structured memory extraction, semantic retrieval, conversational querying, and a FastAPI backend.
Separated LLM-based semantic judgment from deterministic resolution and database state changes.
Implemented duplicate, superseding, coexisting, conflicting, and unrelated memory outcomes.
Evaluated resolution across 25 scenarios: 21 passed (84%), with judgment-sensitive cases documented.

title: LoRA vs. DoRA
subtitle: A rank-8 case study on text-to-SQL
summary: A controlled comparison of rank-8 LoRA and DoRA fine-tuning on Qwen2.5-1.5B for the Spider text-to-SQL task, with repeated seeds and execution-based evaluation.
bullets: Compared identical hyperparameters using execution accuracy on 300 held-out examples.
Repeated experiments across three seeds; 89.7% per-example agreement and query-complexity analysis indicated the accuracy gap was indistinguishable from training noise.
Measured approximately 20% lower DoRA training throughput and traced the cost to per-step weight-norm computation.
Documented methodology, results, and reproducible evaluation tooling.

title: RAG & Agentic AI System
subtitle: Grounded retrieval and tool-calling workflows
summary: A modular retrieval-augmented generation and tool-calling system built from first principles, evaluated for correctness, grounding, hallucination, and completeness.
bullets: Built modular RAG workflows with Sentence Transformers and FAISS, then migrated the architecture to LangChain.
Created a gold-question evaluation pipeline with LLM-as-judge scoring and regression tests.
Implemented and evaluated a prompt-injection guardrail.
Exposed the system through a FastAPI REST API with structured request logging.
